name: Binding Invoker
description:
Invoke a source and binding supplied by value, interpreted under the source's exact kind. invokeBinding exchanges the described input and output frames; no native invocation handle is part of this interface. A kind may be defined in writing, privately or in code.

These operations are offered for voluntary adoption by name. Their schemas and descriptions identify the exchanged values and the capability they describe; they do not prescribe an SDK, internal algorithm, validation or recovery policy, or process architecture. Correspondence is an author claim, not verification of an implementation.

Sources and bindings are OpenBindings 0.2 values. Their core fields have their core meanings and types; x- members are extensions. Source and binding content preserve absence versus JSON null and are interpreted under the source's exact kind. The open carrier schemas are not complete document-conformance checks. Handling malformed carriers is implementation policy; it does not make those carriers conformant.

SupportedKind.description: A kind supported for the work this interface performs.

kind.description: Exact, opaque kind as carried by a source.

KindSupportVerdict.description: Authoritative support verdict for one exact kind. Future optional fields may annotate the verdict but never qualify or soften supported.

kind.description: The exact kind supplied by the caller.

supported.description: True reports that this implementation knows how to interpret this exact kind for its job; it does not promise that every case succeeds. False reports no support for that job.

Source.description: A source as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it: an exact kind and optional content read under that kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core source fields and x- extensions may appear; the open carrier schema does not fully check that boundary. Handling malformed carriers is implementation policy.

kind.description: The source's kind, compared by exact equality.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the source has none.

BindingContext.description: Opaque context supplied by value for one binding invocation. The contract neither requires nor exposes a context store; callers may assemble this object from per-call values, durable state, a credential broker, or any other source before invocation. The general named-credential field is 'credentials': an object keyed by a requirement's nonempty 'name'. For auth.bearer and auth.apiKey its named value is a string; for auth.basic it is an object with username and password; for auth.oauth2 it is an object whose accessToken is the applying credential and whose refreshToken, expiresAt, and clientSecret are optional lifecycle values. Unnamed or unambiguous single-scheme conveniences remain 'bearerToken', 'apiKey', 'basic', and 'accessToken' / 'refreshToken' / 'expiresAt'; the historical 'apiKeys' named map remains accepted for auth.apiKey. Well-known transport fields: 'headers' / 'cookies' / 'environment' (objects with string values) and 'metadata' (object with arbitrary values). Well-known configuration field: 'configuration' (object), keyed by configuration-point name and interpreted by the authority that defines each point. A config.value requirement's JSON Pointer path addresses within configuration[point]; an empty path addresses the entire point. Implementations and callers MAY add fields for session state, consent, or other runtime data; fields without a meaning defined here or by the kind have implementation-specific interpretation. Every value in credentials and the single-scheme credential fields is secret, and any other field may also be secret according to its requirement family, source's kind, or application policy.

ContextRequirement.description: One prerequisite that must be satisfied before a binding can be invoked. `type` names the requirement family; the remaining fields are type-specific. A named well-known `auth.*` requirement resolves at BindingContext.credentials[name]: a string for `auth.bearer` and `auth.apiKey`, a username/password object for `auth.basic`, or an OAuth object beginning with accessToken for `auth.oauth2`. Unnamed or unambiguous single-scheme requirements use the corresponding bearerToken, apiKey, basic, or flat OAuth conveniences; historical apiKeys[name] remains accepted for `auth.apiKey`. OAuth requirements may carry flow fields such as grantType, authorizeUrl, tokenUrl, and scopes. The `config.value` family carries a configuration value a binding needs but the artifact does not supply: it carries 'point' and a JSON Pointer 'path' (plus an optional engine-asserted 'schema') and resolves within BindingContext.configuration. Other families (e.g. 'approval.user', 'account.link') resolve into their own context fields. Resolution architecture and value secrecy beyond the always-secret credential fields are determined by the requirement family, source's kind, and caller.

type.description: Requirement family identifier, such as auth.bearer, auth.oauth2, auth.basic, auth.apiKey, approval.user or config.value. A challenge describes context the producer can apply to this interaction. Unknown families have only their independently defined meanings; the caller decides whether it can satisfy them.

name.description: The scheme name as the source artifact declares it (e.g. an OpenAPI securitySchemes key). Distinguishes multiple requirements of the same family and keys scheme-scoped lookup in BindingContext.credentials.

point.description: config.value only: the configuration point the source's kind defines ('server', 'address', a kind's decode point, …).

path.description: config.value only: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer evaluated from configuration[point]. The empty pointer addresses the whole point; '/variables/region' addresses a nested member; '/value' addresses a member literally named value.

schema.description: config.value only: optional JSON Schema (object or Boolean) describing the value at configuration[point] and path. Read as a standalone schema resource, using JSON Schema 2020-12 unless its root declares another dialect with $schema. References follow the applicable JSON Schema dialect, including resource boundaries introduced by $id. The source artifact and the OBI supply no implicit reference environment. Absence states no constraint. This describes the value, not a required validator, resource-fetching policy or resolution procedure.

description.description: Human-readable description shown to a user or operator during resolution (e.g. an approval prompt message).

durable.description: Whether the producer describes resolved context as suitable for reuse (true) or only for the immediate attempt (false, the default). This is a reuse-safety claim, not a storage instruction; it supplies no store, key, trust decision or persistence policy.

ContextRequiredDetails.description: The data of a CONTEXT_REQUIRED error or a preflight result. alternatives are disjunctive; requirements within one alternative are conjunctive. The object describes the context requested for one invocation, not permission to disclose unrelated credentials. Resolution, trust, storage and retry decisions belong to the caller.

target.description: Opaque identifier for the destination or context scope asserted by the invoker. The identifier is not proof of identity or permission to release a secret. Interpretation follows the source kind; trust decisions, normalization and storage keying belong to the caller.

alternatives.description: Alternative ways to satisfy the reported context requirement (OR). Each alternative describes the requirements needed together (AND). The challenge makes no trust or authorization decision for the caller.

requirements.description: Conjunctive set: every requirement in this alternative must be resolved for the alternative to be satisfied.

InvocationError.description: Unsuccessful-completion record carried by an error frame. The frame kind signals failure independently of the code. Codes defined by the invocation interfaces retain their documented meanings; kind-defined codes have that kind's meaning, and other strings have implementation-specific meaning. ERR_REFUSED asserts no observable effect of the requested operation; CONTEXT_REQUIRED additionally carries the context challenge and asserts no operation output. ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED reports failure without a claim about effects, dispatch, blame, retryability or protocol category. Choosing whether to trust or act on an error is consumer policy.

code.description: Machine-readable reason. Binding invocation owns CONTEXT_REQUIRED (context requested, no operation output or effects), ERR_REFUSED (no operation effects), ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED (failure making no claim about effects or dispatch), ERR_FRAME_PROTOCOL (reported frame-exchange violation), ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED (transport ended before a terminal outcome), and ERR_CANCELLED (caller cancellation, with no rollback or external-stop claim). Operation invocation additionally owns ERR_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND (unresolved operation), ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND (unresolved allowed binding), ERR_BINDING_SELECTION_REQUIRED (ambiguous binding choice), ERR_UNKNOWN_SOURCE (unresolved selected source), ERR_OPERATION_VALIDATION_FAILED (value violates a declared schema), and ERR_SCHEMA_UNRESOLVED (validity could not be determined). These meanings do not prescribe detection, recovery or precedence. Other codes have kind-defined or implementation-specific meanings.

data.description: Optional portable JSON data associated with the unsuccessful completion. A rule defining `code` may define its structure and semantics; otherwise, the source's kind may use it to preserve an opaque application-authored failure value. For CONTEXT_REQUIRED, this is a ContextRequiredDetails object. Presence is significant: an absent member means no portable associated value, while an explicit null is a present JSON null value. Statuses, headers, trailers, envelopes, raw debugging bytes, exception prose, stacks, and implementation evidence do not belong here unless they are themselves application data under an explicit governing rule.

BindingInvocationInput.description: Initial open-frame payload: source and binding by value, and context to apply.

BindingInvokerInputFrame.description: Caller messages: open introduces the invocation request, input carries a value and close ends caller input. The exchange begins with one open; close is optional when input or invocation has already ended. Repeated close has the same meaning. Handling messages outside the described exchange is implementation policy.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the underlying binding. The value's schema is determined by the underlying binding's operation, not by this contract.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller half-close: no further input values. It does not itself report operation completion. Repetition has the same meaning.

BindingInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from the service back to the caller. The service streams a sequence: zero or more non-terminal frames (`output`, `input_closed`) followed by exactly one terminal frame (`complete` or `error`).

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the underlying binding. The value's schema is determined by the underlying binding's operation, not by this contract.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: The invoked binding is no longer accepting input. This is not a terminal outcome; outputs may still follow. Handling subsequent caller frames is implementation policy.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the underlying binding completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the underlying binding failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

Binding.description: A binding as an OpenBindings 0.2 document carries it, or would carry it, by value. It is interpreted under the accompanying source's kind. Absent content and present JSON null are distinct. Only core binding fields and x- extensions may appear; the open carrier schema does not fully check that boundary. Handling malformed carriers is implementation policy.

operation.description: The author's operation key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

source.description: The author's source key, forwarded verbatim without interpretation by this interface.

content.description: Content read under the source's kind: any JSON value, absent when the binding has none.

idempotent.description: The binding author's idempotency claim, carried as information.

preference.description: The author's preference signal, carried as information.

deprecated.description: The author's deprecation signal, carried as information.

openbindings.binding-invoker.listSupport.description: Return an advisory list of kinds supported for this interface's job. Listed kinds have supported: true in checkKindSupport; absence from the list makes no support claim. This is a capability query, not performance of the job.

openbindings.binding-invoker.checkKindSu.description: Report support for this interface's job for the requested exact kind strings, with one verdict per distinct requested kind in first-occurrence order. supported: true means the implementation knows how to interpret that kind for this job, not that every artifact or case succeeds. supported: false reports no support for that job. Additional fields do not qualify the Boolean. The operation reports capability without performing the requested inspection, synthesis or invocation. Kind equality is the core's exact string equality. Capability detection and representation are implementation choices.

oneKind.description: Illustrative job-specific support query; the example kind is defined for these examples only.

openbindings.binding-invoker.invokeBindi.description:
Invoke the supplied binding and exchange caller-facing values using its kind-defined interpretation. The request carries source, binding and optional context, but no operation declaration. Adaptation requiring an operation schema therefore needs another interface.

The caller sends an open frame carrying the invocation request, followed by input frames and an optional close. close means no further input values; input_closed reports that the invoked binding is no longer accepting input. Repeated close has the same meaning. A caller close is unnecessary when input has already closed or the invocation has ended. The service returns output and input_closed frames followed by one terminal complete or error. complete reports successful completion; error reports unsuccessful completion. No further frames belong to the invocation after its terminal frame. An output value alone does not report success. A late failure does not retract values already delivered or assert that no effects occurred.

Frame schemas describe the messages. Handling malformed frames, late inputs or interrupted transports is implementation policy; ERR_FRAME_PROTOCOL and ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED identify those reported failures. The interface does not prescribe parser order, buffer admission, internal terminal-race arbitration, queue draining, polling or handle disposal. ERR_CANCELLED reports cancellation without promising rollback or that external work has stopped.

CONTEXT_REQUIRED carries ContextRequiredDetails and means that the attempt produced neither operation output nor observable effects of the requested operation. This meaning also applies if supplied context proved unusable. The caller may use a reported alternative to make another attempt; the signal does not require or authorize automatic replay. Requirement family and durable fields describe the requested context and whether reuse is represented as safe; the interface supplies no store, resolver, trust decision or retry policy. auth.bearer, auth.basic, auth.apiKey, auth.oauth2 and config.value use the documented context fields; unknown families have only their independently defined meanings.

ERR_REFUSED means the requested operation had no observable effects; ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED makes no such claim. Other error codes retain the meanings described for them or by their defining kind. The interface does not prescribe how an implementation determines these outcomes.

openText.description: One opening frame for illustrative example.text@1. This kind uses absent source content and binding content echo to return its input string. Further input/output and a terminal outcome belong to this exchange.

textValue.description: Individual value frames within that exchange; not the whole invocation.

completion.description: One possible successful terminal outcome. A preceding output value alone would not report success.

contextChallenge.description: A separate illustrative protected service requests a bearer token. This terminal outcome claims no operation output or effects; target is a producer assertion, not authorization to disclose a token. Whether and how to make another attempt is the caller’s choice.

openbindings.binding-invoker.preflightBi.description: Report context requirements identifiable for a possible invocation, as ContextRequiredDetails, or null for no prediction. Preflight does not perform the requested operation, consume its inputs or produce its outputs. It is advisory: null is a valid result even when invocation will need context; invocation does not depend on prior preflight. An unsuccessful completion reports inability to answer; ERR_REFUSED additionally reports that the same request would be refused without operation effects. Source acquisition, caching and other preparation are implementation choices under the source kind.
